Replay

Slopball Parties and browser play

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Identity and authorityConnection and save settingsVerificationReopening a saved party

Configure RSL_ROOM_SERVICE to expose Create party, Join party, Watch only, Copy invite and Rejoin recent. These controls use Replay's shared Party/Room adapters on native Godot and in the browser. Solo uses a local session. Without a service, native Host/Join/Watch retain their direct connection flow.

For a local service and native game, use separate terminals:

Shell
mkdir -m 700 -p .replay-slopball-data
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x52534c4f50423234 REPLAY_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MODEL=slopball \
REPLAY_ROOM_DB="$PWD/.replay-slopball-data/rooms.sqlite3" \
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_room_service/run.sh
Shell
RSL_ROOM_SERVICE=ws://127.0.0.1:49740 RSL_ROOM_LOCAL=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_slopball/play.sh

Omit REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 when reopening an existing service database. Choose Create party and share the invite. Other players paste it and choose Join party; Watch only joins as an observer. The first connected player starts the match.

Native launch settings use RSL_* environment variables. Browser settings use the lowercase suffix as URL query parameters, for example room_service, room_local, name, port and latency. Browser multiplayer requires the configured service and uses WebRTC. Profile loading completes before admission. The test runner below prepares and exports a separate Web build.

Identity and authority#

Personal identity/name preferences use the replay-slopball namespace; Party credentials use replay-slopball-rooms. Native Party storage defaults to user://slopball_rooms.sqlite3, overridden by RSL_ROOMS_DB. Browser records use the shared IndexedDB adapters. Credentials are distinct from game state. Rejoin recent uses a stored credential, preserving the member while obtaining a new process incarnation. Personal name and identity survive a browser restart.

The invite admits up to three trusted peers who may host. Watch only selects seat zero and disables succession-checkpoint acceptance in that session. Observers keep their ball solver frozen and cannot submit player actions. Handoff becomes available when the authority has an eligible successor.

Migration restores the approved checkpoint under a newer epoch. The Body2 adapter seeds the new owner's actual solver from the saved pose and momentum before new scoped observations can commit. It does not serialize Godot contact caches. An abrupt loss can roll back recent progress to the approved backup.

Connection and save settings#

  • RSL_ROOM_ADDRESS and RSL_PORT describe native gameplay reachability; default gameplay port is 49570. The grant supplies the Room connection information.
  • RSL_ROOM_LOCAL=1 permits the shared literal-loopback WS development exception. Secure deployments use the service's normal WSS configuration. RSL_ROOM_CA supplies a native trusted certificate when needed.
  • RSL_ICE_JSON and RSL_ROOM_RELAY configure existing RTC/relay adapters.
  • Save/F5 in a Party publishes through the service, reporting a committed receipt. RSL_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS optionally requests automatic publication. A later successful save replaces that room's published progress.
  • Party publication is separate from native file saves and browser-local storage. Standalone native Save/Resume keeps its matching-profile policy. Browser-local Solo saves are described in the session guide.

The operator-selected slopball service backend validates complete B24 (0x52534c4f50423234) checkpoints. Client requests cannot choose validation code. This integration does not change the model or checkpoint schema.

Verification#

Shell
REPLAY_SLOPBALL_ONLINE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output \
  nix develop --command bash tests/replay_slopball_online/run.sh

The fixture covers native Party UI and four-browser planned/crash migration, including exact recovery, moving solver seeding, continued kicks/goals, observer rejoin, fresh host return, named chat, common world digests and durable publication. It checks actual RTC traffic and rejects WebGL errors. RSL_PROBE=1 enables the extra checkpoint diagnostics used by the browser fixture.

Static pitch, kicker and ball geometry uses authored immutable meshes to avoid Polygon2D redraw buffer conflicts in the pinned Web renderer. Geometry and physics remain the same. Public deployment, broader network/OS/hardware testing, repeated failures, Steam and human play comparison remain roadmap work.

See recorded results and limitations.

Reopening a saved party#

After every game process has stopped, Rejoin recent can reopen the service's published progress under a new authority epoch. Keep the service database and the returning members' Party credentials. The service can restart with database creation disabled. An observer may register first but cannot create an authority runtime; a returning trusted player restores the publication and players reclaim their saved seats.

The saved world includes ownership scopes, accepted body observations, movement baselines, pose, linear/angular velocity, score and names. The first eligible local solver receives that saved pose/momentum before publishing in the new epoch. The UI reports restored progress and known rolled-back ticks. New play can publish a replacement save. Progress after the publication can be lost, and cosmetic chat history is not guaranteed after every process disappears.

Native WSS/ENet and browser RTC shutdown/restart fixtures are available in the native gate and the browser gate. They compare the saved world and actual first solver seed independently, then require another kick/goal, returning named players/observer, new chat and renewed publication.

See shutdown-recovery results and limitations.

The restore gates also cover a trusted player in seat two restoring before the creator returns. The creator subsequently reclaims seat one; the new authority can continue play and publish a replacement checkpoint under its own identity.

See the expanded recovery matrix and its limits.

The recovery notice uses the shared backup-status observation. It distinguishes an approved backup from preparation, stale progress or uncertain control; a prior host change does not imply the next backup is ready.
